assessments.reasoning: The potential-definition list requires source-defined same-name matching. An enclosing scope qualifies by containment without an order condition. A separate potential definition in the same scope must occur earlier in the defined program order, while the identical occurrence is its own expressly listed case.

challenge.method: Compare the enclosing, same-scope and same-instance alternatives and their separate selection rule. Inspect nonstandard traversal cases, special names, and use of unset variables.
challenge.results: Enclosing candidates have no predecessor condition in this rule. The distinct same-scope case requires preceding program order, which is traversal rather than simply textual order. Neither establishes selected or already assigned values.

limitations: Ordinary identifiers at the cited draft only. Same-instance, namespace-field, special-name and runtime initialization rules retain their own scopes.
